profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap point, tagged telecom=data_center, is named "Factory Software | AVEVA Select Italia." AVEVA is a real, publicly traded industrial software company, listed on the London Stock Exchange, that provides engineering design, operations management, and asset-performance software used across manufacturing, energy, and process industries worldwide. "AVEVA Select" is the branding AVEVA uses for its network of regional reseller and systems-integrator partners, and this record most plausibly identifies an Italian partner office selling and supporting AVEVA's software products under that program, likely operating under the name "Factory Software" as the local reseller entity. A software reseller and integrator's office maintains its own business IT systems but is not a data-center operator; the telecom=data_center tag here is best read as a mistag of the office's own server or IT closet.

reading.body:
This record is a mistagged software reseller office, not a data center, and it carries zero megawatts of load.

The point is tagged telecom=data_center in OpenStreetMap, but the name resolves to an Italian office of AVEVA Select, the regional reseller and systems-integrator program of AVEVA, an industrial software company. A reseller office runs its own business IT, which is the likely origin of the tag. The profile states this directly and the research status is exhausted, so the mistag is the finding rather than an open question.

For AI infrastructure this matters as a data-quality signal. Facility counts assembled from volunteered geographic data will absorb offices, closets, and single servers unless each point is checked against an operator. A site like this one contributes nothing to compute capacity, and its megawatt value of zero is the honest reading rather than a missing measurement.

What the data does not cover is the scale of the problem. One corrected point says nothing about how many other points in the same dataset are mistagged, and no count of verified versus unverified facilities is given. The location itself, near Milan Malpensa airport in Italy, is the only geographic fact here, and it describes an office, not a building that supplies power to AI.
